prompt:
A plan for a software change ends with a table of risks. Decide, for each reference problem, whether any row of the table addresses the same underlying problem (names it as a risk or mitigates it specifically), even if worded differently.

Change request: Deploy new versions with zero downtime: run the database migrations automatically on every deploy and keep the site up while the new container starts.

Reference problems:
1. In app/entrypoint.sh, migrations are preceded by python manage.py flush --no-input; mistakenly copying or adapting this development logic into app/entrypoint.prod.sh will wipe the production PostgreSQL database on every deployment.
2. Running python manage.py migrate automatically while the old web container is still serving traffic will crash the live application whenever a migration introduces backward-incompatible changes, such as renaming or dropping columns and tables.
3. Placing python manage.py migrate inside app/entrypoint.prod.sh will cause concurrent migration race conditions and table lock deadlocks if multiple replicas of the web container are launched simultaneously during rollout.
4. Migrations requiring ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table locks (such as adding non-null columns or altering constraints) will block concurrent read and write queries from the running web container, causing request timeouts on the live site.
5. In nginx/nginx.conf, the upstream is hardcoded to server web:8000;, which Nginx resolves via Docker DNS only at startup; starting a new side-by-side container under a different name or IP will not receive traffic without dynamic DNS re-resolution or an explicit Nginx reload.
6. Neither app/Dockerfile.prod nor docker-compose.prod.yml defines container health checks; without readiness checks, incoming traffic will be routed to the new container while migrations are still executing or before Gunicorn has finished binding to port 8000, triggering 502 Bad Gateway errors.
7. The web and nginx services share staticvolume at /home/app/web/staticfiles; running collectstatic for the new version while the old container is live will overwrite existing assets in place, causing cache mismatches and 404 errors for active user sessions.
8. Standard docker-compose commands do not natively support zero-downtime rolling replacements; attempting to start a new web container alongside the existing one will fail due to container name and network alias conflicts unless a blue-green orchestration strategy is introduced.
9. If an automatic database migration fails midway due to a constraint violation or invalid SQL, the deployment script may crash without an automated rollback strategy, leaving the database partially migrated and both container versions in a broken state.
10. When the old web container is terminated after the new one is up, in-flight operations—such as image uploads processed by upload/views.py—will be abruptly severed if Docker does not allow Gunicorn sufficient graceful shutdown time.
11. The script uses a simple nc loop with no timeout to wait for PostgreSQL; if the database never becomes reachable, the container will hang indefinitely, preventing new deployments from completing.

Rows of the risk table:
-  New schema breaks the old container still serving   Old and new code share one DB during the swap   Add-then-remove migrations; review check; removals only in a later release  
-  `migrate` runs in several places at once   Putting it in the entrypoint runs it in every container   One-off release step, never in the entrypoint  
-  nginx keeps using the old container's address   It looks up `web` only at start or reload   Disconnect the old container, reload nginx, then stop it  
-  In-flight uploads are cut off   Retries don't cover POSTs, and the default stop timeout is 10s   Drain first; 30s graceful shutdown under a 35s stop timeout  
-  Migration locks a busy table or fails halfway   Postgres schema changes take exclusive locks   Lock timeout on the migrate run only; backup first; stop on failure  
-  Dev entrypoint copied into prod wipes the DB   `entrypoint.sh` runs `flush --no-input`   Prod entrypoint never migrates; check blocks `flush`  
-  Static files missing or mismatched between versions   Prod never ran `collectstatic`; the static volume is shared   Hashed file names; `collectstatic` without `--clear` in the release step  
-  Script dies mid-swap and leaves two containers   No cleanup on failure   Cleanup trap, deploy lock, old container's ID recorded  
-  Fixing DEBUG causes new errors (500s)   Hashed static files fail hard once DEBUG is off   Fix DEBUG first; run D06 with `DEBUG=0`  
-  Disk fills with images and backups   Every deploy adds an image tag and a DB dump   Keep the last 3 images and 7 dumps
